headline: Advance Day-Use Reservations for the Frio River
reservation: Daily entry permits often sell out weeks in advance for summer weekends and major holidays; securing a day pass or overnight reservation is mandatory for entry. Campground and cabin bookings typically open five months ahead and require a separate process from day-use permits. Always verify current availability through the Texas Parks and Wildlife official system before arrival to ensure park access.

days.title: Canyons and River Heights

stops.name: Old Baldy Summit
stops.detail: Ascend this iconic limestone peak for a 360-degree panorama of the Frio River canyon and Hill Country ridges.

stops.name: Bridges Trail
stops.detail: Traverse the higher elevations of the park to view the rugged Edwards Plateau geology and local bird habitats.

days.driving: Allow 20 minutes from local gateways; conditions vary by season
days.note: The hike to Old Baldy is steep and rocky; morning starts are advised to avoid peak heat.

days.title: Frio River Currents

stops.name: The Frio River Boathouse
stops.detail: Rent a kayak or pedal boat to navigate the clear waters beneath ancient cypress trees.

stops.name: Garner Visitor Center
stops.detail: Learn about the Civilian Conservation Corps history and the stone architecture that defines the park's aesthetic.

days.driving: Allow 30 minutes; traffic may increase during summer weekends
days.note: River flow rates vary significantly based on recent rainfall; check official status at the boathouse.

days.title: Historic Traditions and Lowland Trails

stops.name: Blinn River Trail
stops.detail: Walk the gentle riverbank path to observe Green Kingfishers and white-tailed deer in the bottomlands.

stops.name: The Pavilion
stops.detail: Visit the historic stone structure, famous for nightly jukebox dances that have occurred since the 1940s.

days.driving: Allow 45 minutes from regional hubs; conditions vary
days.note: Pavilion dances are typically seasonal; check the official park bulletin for current event schedules.

intel.title: Lot Capacity
intel.text: Parking near the riverfront and pavilion fills quickly during peak summer days. Arrive early even with a permit to secure a spot close to your planned activity area.

intel.title: Connectivity Limits
intel.text: Cellular reception is highly inconsistent within the deep limestone canyons. Download trail maps and permit confirmations at the gateway cities before entering the park.

intel.title: Gateway Supplies
intel.text: Full service stations are located in the nearby towns of Concan and Leakey. Ensure your tank is sufficient for local canyon driving as no fuel is sold inside the park.

intel.title: Seasonal Foliage
intel.text: Late autumn brings a dramatic color change to the Bald Cypress trees along the Frio River. Target October or November for the rusty orange foliage against the limestone bluffs.

intel.title: Flash Flood Awareness
intel.text: The Frio River is subject to rapid water rises during heavy Hill Country rains. Monitor official weather alerts and obey all low-water crossing closures for safety.

plan.arrival: Rental pickup at San Antonio (SAT) followed by a supply stop in Uvalde for groceries before checking in at the Garner Visitor Center.
plan.vehicle: Standard vehicles are suitable for paved park roads; check rental agreements for any restrictions on unpaved campground access.
plan.goldenHour: Old Baldy Summit offers expansive views for sunset, though colors vary by time of year.
